## Three ways to run the notebooks

Every notebook starts with the same setup cell. It works out where it is running,
fetches the repository if it has to, installs only what is missing, and puts the
caches somewhere sensible. **You do not have to edit anything to switch platforms.**

:::: {.panel-tabset}

## Google Colab

Nothing to install. Click the *Open in Colab* badge on a notebook below, then run
the first cell — it clones this repository into the session for you.

Colab wipes its disk when the runtime is recycled, so model weights are
re-downloaded in a new session. To keep them, change the last line of the setup
cell to:

```python
setup("torch", "transformers", drive=True)
```

and approve the Google Drive prompt. The caches then live in `MyDrive/atrium-school`.

::: {.callout-note}
The restricted datasets (satellite, rock art) are mounted on the school
JupyterHub and are not downloadable. Those case studies need the hub; everything
else runs anywhere.
:::

## School JupyterHub

Nothing to install, and nothing to spawn. We will give you a URL on the first
morning; open it and you are in JupyterLab with the server already running and
this repository already there.

Open `materials/` in the file browser on the left and double-click the notebook
you need. Run the first cell as usual — on the hub it finds everything in place
and installs nothing.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Your work is saved, the machine is not
Your home directory persists, so notebooks you edit and files you save are still
there tomorrow. The server itself may be restarted between sessions; if a
notebook stops responding, *Kernel → Restart Kernel* and re-run from the top.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
If the URL asks you to choose a server configuration, or you land somewhere that
looks nothing like the above, tell an instructor — do not guess.
:::

::: {.content-hidden}

```
ORGANISERS — this block is stripped from the rendered page.

https://docs.cerit.io/en/docs/web-apps/jupyterhub

Image      Pytorch 2.4.1  — NOT "NVIDIA Pytorch", which is the CUDA/NGC
           build and is far larger than we need.
CPU        2 cores        (4 for the Thursday satellite session)
Memory     8 GB           (16 GB for Thursday)
GPU        none           — everything this week runs on CPU in seconds
Home       persistent, THE SAME directory on every spawn. Only /home/jovyan
           survives a respawn: `pip install --user` puts packages in
           ~/.local and model weights cache in ~/.cache/huggingface, both
           inside it. A fresh home each spawn means every participant
           re-downloads ~600 MB of CLIP weights in front of the room.

Prepare each home once, before the school:
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ARUP-CAS/atrium-school-ml.git
  cd atrium-school-ml && python -m pip install --user -r requirements.txt
  python -c "from transformers import CLIPModel, CLIPProcessor; \
    CLIPModel.from_pretrained('openai/clip-vit-base-patch32'); \
    CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained('openai/clip-vit-base-patch32')"
The last line warms ~/.cache/huggingface so Monday starts instantly.

Restricted data (satellite, rock art) is mounted read-only at
/home/jovyan/shared/<name> — the paths in case-studies/datasets.yml.
Mount it before Thursday; get_dataset() fails with a clear message if it
is missing, but that message is not a substitute for the data.

If participants ever do have to spawn their own server, the settings above
are what they must choose — the wrong image or a new home directory is the
one failure mode that eats a session.
```

## Your own machine

Follow the [setup guide](setup.qmd), then start Jupyter (or open the notebook in
your IDE) anywhere inside the clone:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ARUP-CAS/atrium-school-ml.git
cd atrium-school-ml
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt \
    --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu \
    --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple
```

The setup cell finds the repository around it and installs nothing further.

::::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Datasets are not in the repository
They are too large, and some are not redistributable. Every notebook fetches its
data the same way, and caches it so it is downloaded only once:

```python
from atrium_data import get_dataset
path = get_dataset("coins")
```

Where each dataset actually lives is recorded in
[`case-studies/datasets.yml`](https://github.com/ARUP-CAS/atrium-school-ml/blob/main/case-studies/datasets.yml){.external}.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Work on a copy
Copy a notebook before you edit it (`cp intro.ipynb my-intro.ipynb`). We will push
updates during the week, and `git pull` on a notebook you have changed produces a
merge conflict in raw JSON that nobody enjoys resolving.
:::
